text: . The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has said that India’s efforts to diversify its oil supplies have helped the country cope with disruptions in global energy markets amid the ongoing conflict in West Asia. However, it has cautioned that a prolonged rise in energy prices could create fresh inflationary pressures.In its October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook for Asia and the Pacific, the IMF noted that major Asian economies, including India, Japan and South Korea, have adapted to disruptions in energy markets by securing oil from alternative sources outside West Asia, helping restore supplies to pre-conflict levels. The report said that while these efforts have helped strengthen energy supply resilience, a prolonged energy price shock could increase commodity prices, push up transportation and production costs, and put pressure on household budgets and economic growth.The IMF also observed that prices of refined petroleum products, particularly diesel and aviation fuel, had risen more sharply than crude oil prices following the conflict. This could increase operating costs for businesses and affect consumers.The Fund recommended targeted and time-bound support measures to protect vulnerable households, while cautioning against broad-based fuel subsidies and price controls that could put additional pressure on government finances. Beyond energy markets, the IMF identified uncertainty surrounding investments in artificial intelligence and tighter global financial conditions as other potential risks to regional growth. The report underscores the importance of India’s efforts to diversify energy sources, strengthen economic resilience and maintain stable growth amid global uncertainties..

. The country’s foreign exchange reserves declined over 8.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 726 billion US dollars during the week ended 9th of October. According to Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, dropped by 7.1 billion dollars to 597.6 billion dollars during the week. Gold reserves dropped by 1.3 billion dollars to 105 billion dollars. Special Drawing Rights fell by 109 million dollars to 18.5 billion dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund dipped 10 million dollars to 4.78 billion dollars.

. In cricket, Indian men’s team will face the West Indies in the decisive fifth and final T20 International at M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru this evening. With the five-match series level at two-all. The game is scheduled to begin at 7 PM Indian Standard Time.India will now aim to extend their unbeaten streak in home T20I series, a run dating back to February 2019 when Australia last won a T20I series on Indian soil. A victory for the West Indies, however, would secure their first bilateral T20I series win in India, ending the hosts’ remarkable streak and marking their first series win against India across any format on Indian soil since 2003.Led by Shreyas Iyer, India have added veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar to their squad, resting Jasprit Bumrah.India leads the West Indies 22-12 in their overall T20I head-to-head record, with one match ending in a no result.

. India’s Komal has won a bronze medal in the women’s 59-kilogram category at the Under-23 World Wrestling Championships at Las Vegas in United States. Komal defeated Kazakhstan’s Viktoriia Khusainova 7-2 in the bronze-medal bout to finish third. Earlier, she defeated Canada’s Ella Finding on criteria after a 1-1 draw and overcame Moldova’s Madalina Prisacari 8-3. However, she lost her semifinal bout to Ukraine’s Alina Filipovych by technical superiority.Another wrestler Amruta Pujari has entered the final of the women’s 72-kilogram category after securing two consecutive victories by pinfall. Amruta will face Ukraine’s Iryna Zablotska in the gold-medal bout. Pujari began her campaign with a pinfall victory over Kazakhstan’s Sabyrzhanova before defeating China’s Wenjin Qiu in the semifinal.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has revised the timings and operational framework of the Closing Auction Session in the equity cash market. It has also updated the settlement methodology for stock and index derivatives contracts. Under the new framework, the Closing Auction Session will operate for 10 minutes, from 3.30 PM to 3.40 PM, on all trading days. The session will include different phases for calculating the reference price and placing orders. The order-entry window will close randomly between 3.38 PM and 3.40 PM.Trading in stock and index derivatives will continue until 3.45 PM. On expiry days, however, trading in expiring index derivatives contracts will end at 3.30 PM. Stock derivatives trading will continue until 3.45 PM. The post-closing session in the cash market will run from 3.50 PM to 4 PM, with trades executed at the closing price.SEBI has also revised the method for calculating settlement prices on expiry days. For index derivatives, settlement prices will be based on the underlying index value, calculated using the volume-weighted average prices of constituent stocks during the final 30 minutes of continuous trading. For stock derivatives, settlement prices will be based on the volume-weighted average price of the underlying stock during the same period.The regulator has also specified rules for carrying forward unexecuted orders into the Closing Auction Session. These include provisions for iceberg orders, which will be converted into fully disclosed limit orders, subject to specified conditions. The revised provisions, except those relating to the transition of unexecuted orders, will take effect from 7 December 2026. The provisions concerning unexecuted limit and iceberg orders will come into force on 8 February 2027. SEBI has directed stock exchanges and clearing corporations to make the necessary system and procedural changes in consultation with the regulator within seven days of its circular issued yesterday.

. Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav has informed that India’s Ramsar site tally has reached 103. In a social media post, the Minister said that India continues to strengthen its commitment to wetland conservation, with Sukhna Lake in Chandigarh and Sauj Jheel in Uttar Pradesh becoming the latest additions to the list of Ramsar Sites. Mr Yadav said that this milestone highlights the importance that Narendra Modi government has been laying on wetlands in conserving biodiversity, enhancing water and climate security, and sustaining local livelihoods. He said these additions reaffirm India’s ongoing efforts to conserve its rich wetland ecosystems and strengthen the ecological, climatic and livelihood benefits they provide. The Minister also congratulated Uttar Pradesh and Chandigarh for the achievement.

. Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal has informed that all 24 Indian seafarers aboard two vessels involved in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and Romania are safe, with no casualties or injuries reported.In a social media post yesterday, Mr Sonowal said crude oil tanker MT ST 3, carrying 15 Indian seafarers, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 15, while chemical tanker YARA J, carrying nine Indian seafarers, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage in Romania on October 14. He said the government is closely monitoring both incidents and coordinating with ship management companies to ensure the safety of the crew members.Earlier, India strongly condemned attacks on maritime navigation and commercial shipping amid escalating tensions in West Asia. Addressing the UN Security Council’s debate on the Middle East, India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, called for immediate de-escalation and urged all parties to resolve the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices closed higher for the second consecutive session today. The Sensex rose 414 points, or 0.56 per cent to end at 74,729. The Nifty climbed 149 points, or 0.65 per cent to settle at 23,146.However, the broader market on the National Stock Exchange underperformed the frontline indices. The Midcap 100 index fell 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index remained largely unchanged.In the Sensex pack, 18 out of 30 constituent companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Tech Mahindra skyrocketed over 8.4 per cent, Tata Consultancy Services gained 4.6 per cent, and Infosys surged more than 4.5 per cent. In contrast, Indigo dropped 2.2 per cent, Reliance slipped 1.1 per cent, and Asian Paints fell one per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 15 out of 28 sectors ended in the negative zone. Among the top laggards, Housing Finance dropped 1.2 per cent, Hospitals slipped 0.8 per cent, and Services dipped 0.7 per cent. In contrast, IT climbed 3.4 per cent, Focused IT advanced 3.3 per cent, and Telecommunication jumped nearly 1.6 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,404 companies advanced, 1,962 declined, and 250 remained unchanged.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India is all set to become a global sporting powerhouse. Interacting with the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Games 2026 in New Delhi, Mr Modi lauded the Asian Games champions, saying they have made the Tricolour fly high. He said their achievements show what passion, perseverance and belief can achieve. Praising the athletes for bringing immense pride to 140 crore citizens, the Prime Minister emphasized that the ultimate achievement lies in elevating the honor and glory of the national flag. He congratulated the players, their coaches, support staff, and families for this collective national triumph.Recalling the historic milestones achieved at the Asian Games, the Prime Minister celebrated the double Gold victory of the men’s and women’s hockey teams, with the women ending a 44-year wait. He highlighted the consecutive medals for both cricket teams and dual Golds in Kabaddi. He also lauded the five Golds in archery, stellar displays in shooting, boxing, and wrestling, new athletics records, a weightlifting medal after 28 years, and the first marathon success since 1982.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports, Raksha Khadse and President of the Indian Olympic Association P T Usha were also present on the occasion.India finished fourth in the medal tally at the Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, winning 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. This marked India’s second consecutive finish among the top five nations at the Asian Games, reflecting the country’s growing competitiveness across a diverse range of sporting disciplines.

. More than 1 lakh 93 thousand additional houses have been approved under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0). With this approval, the total number of houses sanctioned under the Mission now exceeds 20 lakhs. The Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs made this announcement yesterday following the 10th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee in New Delhi, chaired by Department of Urban Development Secretary Satendra Singh.The Ministry highlighted that these houses have been sanctioned under the Beneficiary-Led Construction and Affordable Housing in Partnership verticals of PMAY-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal. These houses are intended for eligible urban families belonging to the Economically Weaker Section.During the meeting, the Secretary underscored the need for close coordination among the Ministry, States, Union Territories, and Urban Local Bodies to ensure timely submission and processing of housing proposals.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was 0.3 per cent up at 1,46,426 rupees per 10 grams. Silver surged over 1.2 per cent to 2,10,918 rupees per kilogram.

. The AYUSH Ministry has issued standard treatment guidelines on Management of Dermatological Disorders for Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy, with the inclusion of Yoga. The document has been prepared by the Ayush Vertical of the Directorate General of Health Services and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The Ministry said that the document is intended to bring more uniformity, quality assurance and evidence-informed practice to clinical care across the Ayush systems. Ayush Minister Prataprao Jadhav underlined that these guidelines will deepen the integration of Ayush systems with the national healthcare framework. He said that by promoting standardised and evidence-informed clinical practice, the guiidelines will contribute to improving patient care and strengthening the role of Ayush systems in public health.

. US President Donald Trump has waived the application of sanctions, restrictions and duties under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, citing the national interest of the United States. In an order issued on yesterday evening, Trump said he had submitted a certification to the Congress stating that the waiver was in the national interest of the country.The legislation empowers the US administration to impose sweeping sanctions on Russia and steep tariffs on major purchasers of Russian oil and gas, including India and China. The waiver comes amid continued scrutiny of Russian energy exports and US efforts to use economic measures against Moscow and countries purchasing its oil and gas.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. Today is World Cotton Day. This day is celebrated annually on October 7 to highlight the global economic, social, and environmental importance of cotton. The theme for this year is Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Sharing a video message, Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh extended greetings to everyone associated with this sector.He said that this day honours farmers who cultivate cotton in the fields, thereby enabling employment for workers across the entire value chain, whether in spinning mills, ginneries, textile manufacturing units, or garment factories. He informed that 60 lakh farmers in the country are engaged in cotton cultivation. He underlined that countless small enterprises are linked to the handloom industries that not only operate domestically but also export their products.

. The Centre has made Aadhaar authentication or proof of possession of an Aadhaar number necessary to avail of scholarship benefits under the PM CARES for Children Scheme. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has issued a notification in this regard. It said that beneficiaries of the Special Scholarship Scheme under PM CARES for Children, which provides assistance for continuing education from Class 1st to 12th, will be required to undergo Aadhaar authentication or furnish proof of possession of an Aadhaar number.The notification stated that no child will be denied assistance for failure to authenticate Aadhaar or for not having been assigned an Aadhaar number. In such cases, the benefit will be provided after verifying the child’s identity and establishing the relationship with the parent or legal guardian through the documents specified in the notification. Our correspondent has the details.The notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment provides separate document requirements for beneficiaries below 18 years of age and those aged 18 years or above who have not been assigned an Aadhaar number. Children below 18 years of age can establish their identity by submitting an enrolment acknowledgement containing the Enrolment ID and a document establishing their age, such as a birth certificate, Indian passport or a Class 10th or Class 12th certificate or marks statement issued by a recognised school education board.For beneficiaries aged 18 or above, the notification lists documents such as an Election Commission-issued voter identity card, driving license, Indian passport, and ration card, along with other specified identity documents. The notification also provides for alternative authentication methods, including biometric or one-time password-based verification, wherever feasible, if Aadhaar authentication fails.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has offered prayers to Maa Kalratri, marking the seventh day of Navratri today. In a social media post, he expressed hope that the blessings of Maa Kalratri would illuminate everyone’s life with new energy and renewed confidence. Mr Modi prayed that, by the divine grace of the Goddess, prosperity and well-being would prevail for all.

. The Digital India BHASHINI Division and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, have developed text-to-speech (TTS) models for Sourashtra, a minority Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by the Sourashtra community in Tamil Nadu. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology said the initiative aims to expand the availability of speech technology for languages with limited digital resources. It will also support the use of these languages in digital applications, language learning, accessibility solutions, documentation, and research. According to the Ministry, the newly developed models use a Variational Inference with Adversarial Learning-based end-to-end text-to-speech architecture, enabling them to generate Sourashtra speech directly from text. The models feature both male and female voices, with each voice supporting text written in both Tamil and Sourashtra scripts. This enables users to access and use Sourashtra in the scripts commonly used to write the language.

. In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by nine paise to close at 94.96 rupees against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 101.66 in intra-day trade.

. In the United States, three children and a teacher were killed in a shooting at a primary school in the state of Oregon. Police said a 16-year-old attacker forced his way into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend on Thursday afternoon. The children killed in the incident were aged five, eight and eleven. The attacker was also killed after a community member confronted him inside the school. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek praised the community members for intervening and helping prevent further loss of life.

. In Badminton, India’s Jagsher Singh Khangurra has secured a bronze medal at the BWF World Junior Championships in Cairo, Egypt. He settled for third place after losing his Men’s singles semifinal to Indonesia’s Radithya Bayu Wardhana, 6-15, 15-13, 3-15 today.Yesterday, Khangurra defeated Yuan-Syue Jhuang of Chinese Taipei 6-15, 17-15, 15-12 to reach the semifinals.The bronze medal is India’s seventh in the individual events at the World Junior Championships. It takes the country’s overall medal tally to 13, comprising one gold, five silver and seven bronze medals.

. In a fresh advisory issued in view of the prevailing situation, the Embassy of India in Riyadh today advised Indians planning to travel to Saudi Arabia, including for Umrah, to take into account the ongoing disruptions at Saudi airports and the possibility of flight cancellations, which could result in extended stays.It also advised Indian nationals to continue following instructions issued by local authorities and remain indoors in the event of an aerial attack. The Embassy urged Indian nationals to refrain from filming, publishing or sharing any information, photographs or videos related to the ongoing events.Meanwhile, Riyadh International Airport remains closed to flight operations, while airports in Dammam, Jeddah and Medina remain operational, although some disruptions continue. The Embassy said Saudia Airlines continues to operate scheduled flights to Indian destinations from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. It added that Indian nationals requiring urgent departure may consider travelling via Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar, subject to obtaining the necessary visas.

. The Maldives has expressed its appreciation to India for the decision to roll over the first withdrawal of 30 billion rupees under the Indian rupee currency swap agreement, saying the move reaffirms the longstanding bonds of friendship between the two countries. Maldivian Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam thanked External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and the Government for the decision.In a post on X yesterday, she said the decision reaffirms the longstanding bonds of friendship between Maldives and India, rooted in mutual respect, understanding, and goodwill. Earlier on the day, India approved the request of the Maldives government for the rollover of a 30 billion rupee currency swap facility as part of New Delhi’s ‘Neighbours First’ policy and the commitment to deepening bilateral relations with the island nation, according to an official statement.The facility is being extended under the Framework on Currency Swap Arrangement for SAARC countries, signed between the Reserve Bank of India and the Maldives Monetary Authority during Maldivian President Mohamed Muizzu’s state visit to India in October 2024. The first drawdown of 30 billion rupees was extended to the Maldivian government on April 23 this year.The currency swap arrangement provides the Maldives with access to Indian rupees, helping support liquidity and financial stability when needed. For India, continued financial assistance also forms part of its broader engagement with a strategically important Indian Ocean neighbour.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Located at Teen Murti Marg in New Delhi, the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya inspires the younger generation by showcasing the vision, leadership and contributions of all the Prime Ministers.Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya, inaugurated by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2022, highlights the contributions of all the Prime Ministers to the nation’s development. The museum showcases how Indian democracy has provided opportunities for leaders from every section of society to contribute to nation-building. Spread across two buildings, the modern digital museum offers visitors an insight into India’s political history, democratic traditions and journey of development. The Sangrahalaya features a Light and Sound Show titled ‘Veeranganaon ki Mahagatha’, which narrates the inspiring stories of valiant women warriors who fought to uphold the nation’s pride. Inaugurating the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya, Prime Minister Modi described the museum as a living symbol of the shared heritage and collective contributions of all governments.During his visit to the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya, Justice S. Thurairaja of Sri Lanka shared his reflections on India’s democratic journey and the leadership that has shaped the nation.

. Secretary in the External Affairs Ministry, Sudhakar Dalela, has been appointed as the next Ambassador of India to Nepal. Mr Dalela is a 1993 batch Indian Foreign Service officer. The External Affairs Ministry said that he is expected to take up the assignment shortly

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today met Governor of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation, Kazuhiko Amakawa, on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok. The two sides discussed expanding cooperation in clean energy, semiconductors and critical minerals. In a social media post, Finance Ministry said, the discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in energy transition, advanced manufacturing, electric mobility and resilient supply chains. They also explored cooperation through the 600-million-dollar India-Japan Fund and Japanese participation in the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund.During the meeting, Ms Sitharaman encouraged Japanese investors to explore opportunities in data centres in Tier Two and Tier Three cities, including Visakhapatnam. She said such investments could help promote more balanced urban development.Mr Amakawa highlighted the success of the India-Japan Fund in electric mobility and bioethanol. He also expressed hope for a follow-on fund and noted growing Japanese interest in semiconductors, artificial intelligence and data centres.The Finance Minister is on a five-day official visit to Bangkok in Thailand, till 18th of this month to attend the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings.

. BJP President Nitin Nabin has strongly criticised the opposition, accusing it of attempting to destabilise the country in collusion with foreign powers. In a social media post, Mr Nabin alleged that the use of the term “regime change” exposed its agenda. He also alleged that the opposition’s fight is not for electoral reforms, the SIR, or the future of the country’s youth, but rather to spread anarchy in the country and seize power at any cost.  He said, in democracy, the path to power passes through the mandate of the people, not through chaos. Mr Nabin added that India’s citizens and the BJP will never allow any attempt to weaken the country’s democratic system to succeed.Meanwhile, addressing a press conference in New Delhi, BJP Spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi alleged that the use of terms like ‘Regime Change’ points towards attempts to create a situation of unrest in India. He claimed that organising protests in Central Delhi during the ongoing festival season can be aimed at harming the country’s growing economy.

. Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri highlighted India’s resilience amidst global economic turbulence and geopolitical disruptions. He noted that the country successfully maintained the continuity of essential fuel supplies during recent West Asian crisis by diversifying energy sources and bolstering domestic capacities.Mr Puri said this while addressing the national conference on ‘Pathways to Viksit Bharat: A Centenary Conclave’ organised by Shri Ram College of Commerce in New Delhi yesterday. He also expressed confidence that the youth entering their professional prime will drive India towards becoming a developed nation.Recalling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent visit to the SRCC, Mr Puri urged the youth to aspire to make Indian enterprises global leaders. He also called upon youth to build world-class Indian institutions and enterprises based on reliability, innovation and international trust.

. US President Donald Trump has said that his priority is to end the Russia-Ukraine war, asserting that both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy want the conflict to end. However, Zelenskyy has accused Moscow of showing no genuine willingness to negotiate, amid continued hostilities and differences over sanctions and security guarantees.Speaking to the media, Trump said he was focused on bringing the war to an end, citing the heavy casualties on both sides.Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said Putin was using rhetoric that did not reflect a genuine desire for peace. In a social media post, the Ukrainian President said Moscow was not interested in negotiations at present and was merely engaging in word games.

. A white paper, released by the Confederation of Indian Industry – CII, has said that India needs to accelerate growth in its media and entertainment sector to roughly 15 percent annually, to reach its 100 billion dollar ambition by the early 2030s. With the current 9 percent annual growth rate, the sector would reach only about 64 billion dollars by 2033, leaving a revenue gap of USD 36 billion.Released at the CII Big Picture Summit 2026 in Mumbai today, the white paper titled ‘The New Economics of Media & Entertainment’, lists market-led broadcasting, measurable action against piracy, and investment in regional markets and emerging businesses as immediate priorities to achieve the goal.Speaking on the occasion, Summit Chair and MD & CEO, Sony Pictures Networks,  Gaurav Banerjee said India has achieved audience scale; the next imperative is to create, capture and retain greater value from it. He added that CII is seeking greater freedom over television pricing and packaging, removal of carriage fees, restored audience measurement, and transparent standards across screens. It has further proposed reducing GST on television, OTT and music subscriptions to 5 percent, alongside proportionate regulation and industry self-regulation.The paper states that the next phase of growth will come from new technologies and business models, including responsible AI, virtual production, connected TV and creator-led formats and from industries beyond entertainment that need Indian studios’ animation, gaming, XR and digital-mapping skills.Considering that India has about 6.8 cinema screens per million people with Bihar and Uttar Pradesh having the lowest screen densities, CII has proposed setting up over 16 thousand screens by early 2030 while promoting regional-language content, connectivity and local creative talent.<>

. India has reiterated that energy security remains a key priority amid US sanctions, with a focus on ensuring reliable supplies at competitive prices for its 1.4 billion people. Indian Ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar has also expressed confidence that bilateral trade between the two countries will reach 100 billion US dollars by 2030. Kumar said India’s energy procurement decisions are guided by national interests, diversified sources and the need for affordable and predictable supplies. He also pointed out that Europe had imported more than 320 billion US dollars’ worth of Russian energy resources since 2022.

. Newly appointed Indian Ambassador Abhay Kumar presented his credentials to the President of Azerbaijan, Ilham Aliyev, in Baku. During the meeting yesterday, Ambassador Abhay Kumar conveyed his commitment to working towards the further strengthening and expansion of bilateral relations between India and Azerbaijan. He affirmed that he would spare no effort to promote closer cooperation between the two countries and to deepen the longstanding bonds of friendship and mutual understanding between their peoples.Reference was also made to the interaction between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Ilham Aliyev held in September 2026 in Bishkek, on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi surged over two per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 jumped 1.4 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose half a per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex added 0.3 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite as well as Singapore’s Strait Times gained over 0.2 per cent each.In European markets, Germany’s DAX soared one per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 added 0.1 per cent, when reports last came in.

. US President Donald Trump has backed Israel’s offer to assist Saudi Arabia in countering Houthi rebel attacks, describing Israel’s support as very helpful amid escalating regional hostilities. He also expressed optimism that Saudi Arabia could join the Abraham Accords, which seek to normalise relations between Israel and Arab countries.Speaking to the media yesterday, Trump said Saudi Arabia should accept Israel’s offer of assistance. He also suggested that the prospects of Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords were stronger than ever.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has extended the submission deadline for Stage II of the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge to 22nd of this month. The Ministry said that the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, has received an overwhelming response from across the country. It informed that over 1.45 crore attempts have been recorded in the Viksit Bharat Quiz as part of the selection process. The Ministry added that about 5.7 lakh youth who qualified in the Quiz round have moved to the next stage, the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge, where they must submit a 500-word essay on the MY Bharat portal on the theme designated for their region.The Ministry further advised the youth who have not yet submitted their essays to submit them by the 22nd of this month. It said that the extension gives eligible participants more time to submit their essays and encourages wider participation in this national initiative.

. Media accreditation for the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 has been extended by two days. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting today said that media professionals planning to cover the festival can submit their applications through the official Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation portal till the 17th of this month. The Ministry advised eligible media persons to complete their registration and upload the required documents before the revised deadline.The 57th edition of IFFI 2026 will be held from 20th to 28th of next month, in Panaji, Goa.

. In women’s cricket, hosts India defeated Zimbabwe by four wickets in the first T20 International of the three-match series in Raipur.Put into bat first, Zimbabwe scored 114 for five in their allotted 20 overs. In reply, India chased down the target in just 15.4 overs, losing six wickets.The victory extended India’s winning streak to six consecutive matches.In a special initiative, female spectators have been allowed free entry to all three T20 Internationals following a suggestion by Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai.The second T20 International will be played tomorrow, while the third match is scheduled for the 20th of this month.The T20I series will be followed by a three-match One Day International series, with the matches scheduled to be played in Vadodara on the 23rd, 25th and 28th of this month.

. Yemen’s government has accused the Houthis of targeting Aden International Airport with two missiles, which reportedly landed near a Yemenia Airlines aircraft preparing for takeoff to Cairo. In a social media post, Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar Al-Eryani yesterday said flight IY 612 was preparing to depart for Cairo International Airport when the missiles landed around 500 metres from the aircraft and 100 metres from the runway’s centre.Passengers and crew members were reported safe. He described Aden airport as a vital gateway for Yemenis travelling for medical treatment, education and employment.The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia issued a security advisory warning American citizens of possible attacks, airport disruptions, flight cancellations and airspace closures amid recent missile and unmanned aerial vehicle attacks.

. The government has issued revised operational guidelines for the Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs), with enhanced financial support for hosting international sporting events in India. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said the revised scheme provides financial assistance of up to 50 crore rupees for hosting international sporting events in the country. The scheme also provides assistance of up to 50 crore rupees for conducting the National Games. The funding will cover sports equipment, timing, scoring and results services, remuneration for technical officials, and other technical arrangements. The revised guidelines also provide for the establishment of specialised Olympic Training Centres equipped with modern sports science facilities to support elite athletes.The Ministry said the scheme includes assistance for promoting indigenous sports internationally, facilitating training for athletes and coaches from Global South countries at Indian high-performance centres, and organising sporting events, conferences and workshops under multilateral forums such as BRICS and BIMSTEC. Support will also be extended to recognised international and continental sports organisations that have offices in India.The Ministry said the revised scheme aligns with India’s long-term sporting vision and its preparations for the 2036 Olympic bid and the Commonwealth Games 2030.

. The Supreme Court today said it will intervene if frequent protests and security restrictions around Connaught Place in New Delhi adversely affect businesses. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was hearing a plea challenging the New Delhi Municipal Council’s decision to close Central Park for two days ahead of a protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party.Representing traders, the advocate told the Apex Court that the protests were causing significant business losses. The lawyer argued that the restrictions were disproportionate, particularly ahead of the festive season, including Karva Chauth, Dussehra, Diwali and Chhath.Chief Justice Surya Kant acknowledged the difficulties faced by small shopkeepers, hawkers and stall owners, observing that their livelihoods and families were being affected. The Bench said it would exercise its constitutional powers, including those under public law, if the restrictions unlawfully affected businesses.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over  Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for tomorrow. Similar weather conditions are expected over Andhra Pradesh and West Rajasthan.  IMD said that conditions are likely to become favourable for further withdrawal of southwest monsoon from some more parts of eastern India and many parts of northeast India during the next two days. Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Kerala can also experience thunderstorms accompanied with Lightning.

. The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over South Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal today. Heavy rainfall is also expected over Andhra Pradesh, Coastal Karnataka, Kerala and Mahe. The weather agency has predicted thunderstorm accompanied with lightning very likely at isolated places over Chhattisgarh, Coastal Karnataka, Goa, Madhya Pradesh, Marathwada and Odisha today.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has said that cargo movement on inland waterways increased from 29 million metric tonnes in 2014-15 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, registering a compound annual growth rate of 20.13 per cent. The Ministry said the growth has already surpassed the target of 200 million metric tonnes set under Maritime India Vision 2030. India has 111 National Waterways, extending over 20,187 kilometres across 23 states and four Union Territories. The Ministry added that the country is strengthening its inland waterway network through hydrographic surveys, modern navigation infrastructure and digital information systems to support the growing movement of cargo on rivers..

. Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw today met members of the Indian Women’s Kabaddi team in New Delhi. The team won the gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. On the occasion, Mr Vaishnaw congratulated the women sportspersons of Indian Railways on their gold-medal victory. He praised the players for making the country proud through their dedication, determination and sporting excellence.The Railway sportspersons who met the Minister included head coach Neeta Moreshwar Dadwe of South Central Railway, Pooja of Northern Railway and Ritu Negi of South Central Railway, among others. The Ministry of Railways said, through institutional support and opportunities to pursue sporting careers alongside employment, Indian Railways continues to play an important role in nurturing sporting talent across the country.

. The Board of Control for Cricket in India has announced the Indian men’s team squads for the upcoming ODI and Test series against New Zealand. The five-match ODI series begins in Auckland on the 4th of next month, with the final two matches scheduled in Mount Maunganui on 13th and 15th November.Shubman Gill will captain the side in the first three ODIs before leaving to prepare for the Test series. Shreyas Iyer, who has been named vice-captain for the opening three matches, will lead the team in the final two ODIs.Senior batters Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli feature in both ODI squads. Fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah has been rested from the ODI series but included in the Test squad, while all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja has been left out of the ODI teams.Anshul Kamboj has been selected for the first three ODIs, while wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra joins the squad for the final two matches. Prasidh Krishna’s selection for the opening three ODIs is subject to fitness clearance. Gill will also lead India in the Test series, with KL Rahul named vice-captain.

The National Investigation Agency has filed a charge sheet against five accused, including ULFA (I) chief Paresh Baruah, in connection with the recovery of an IED in Assam’s Guwahati on August 15, 2024. The United Liberation Front of Asom-Independent, or ULFA (I), is a banned terrorist outfit.The chargesheet was filed before an NIA special court at Guwahati against Baruah, chairman of the proscribed terrorist organisation ULFA (I), an official statement said. The accused have been named in the chargesheet filed in connection with the NIA’s probe into the recovery of an improvised explosive device at Motilal Nehru Road, Panbazar, Guwahati. They have been charged under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 and the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, said the statement issued by the NIA.The case was initially registered at Panbazar police station in Guwahati on August 16, 2024, and was re-registered by the NIA on February 27 last year.

. In women’s cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe by four wickets in the first T20 International of the three-match series in Raipur last night. Put into bat first, Zimbabwe scored 114 for five in their allotted 20 overs. In reply, India chased down the target in just 15.4 overs, losing six wickets.Deepti Sharma, who scored 49 off 37 balls, was adjudged the player of the match, and Niki Prasad made an unbeaten 39 off 35 balls.This was Smriti Mandhana’s first match as full-time captain of the Indian women’s cricket team. In a special initiative, female spectators have been allowed free entry to all three T20 Internationals following a suggestion by Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai. The second T20 International will be played tomorrow, while the third match is scheduled for the 20th of this month.India and Zimbabwe are playing a bilateral series for the first time. The T20I series will be followed by a three-match One Day International series, with the matches scheduled to be played in Vadodara on the 23rd, 25th, and 28th of this month.

. Indian wrestler Vishvajit Ramchandra More has created history by clinching a historic silver medal in the Greco-Roman finals at the U23 World Championships in Las Vegas today. Competing in the men’s 55kg final, More narrowly lost 12-13 to Georgia’s Koba Karumidze in the final seconds of the bout.​This marks India’s first-ever silver medal and first-ever appearance in a Greco-Roman final at the U23 World Championships. Earlier in the week, the two-time U23 bronze medallist secured his place in the history books by advancing through a challenging draw.​More opened his campaign with a 10-8 victory over Mexico’s Isaac Marin Mata, followed by an 8-1 win against Iran’s U20 world champion Armin Shamsipour in the quarterfinals using a four-pointer throw. He then defeated Russia’s Malik Gigiev 6-4 in a thrilling semifinal encounter to reach the title match.
